Two special types of overlapped block structures which can be used to realized finite impulse response (FIR) filters are discussed. Their efficient implementation based on fast short-length linear convolution algorithms and discrete Fourier transform (DFT) are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Passive ladder synthesis in filtorX
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: With the inclusion of ladder synthesis primitives into the filtorX language, filter designers can use a simple graphical interface to obtain passive ladder prototypes. These design techniques can also be programmed to obtain a means of automated ladder synthesis. A ladder structure derived from a bandpass transfer function highlights the ease of design and illustrates the potential for automation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Arrangements of the secondary source on the performance of active noise control systems
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Three active noise control (ANC) systems, which incorporates different arrangements of the secondary loudspeaker, have been examined experimentally, based on the analysis of the characteristics of sound wave propagation in a duct. Measured transfer functions of the plant and the error paths show good agreement with the theoretically derived transfer functions in the acoustic modal frequencies of the systems. Real-time experiments showed a more effective noise attenuation with a tree-shaped configuration than with the traditional T-shaped ANC system. The symmetric arrangement of two secondary speakers in the tree-shaped system helps in compensating the node observed at 200 Hz in the error path. This compensation can also be achieved by using an equalizer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A hierarchical multiprocessor architecture for video coding applications
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A hierarchical multiprocessor architecture for real-time video coding applications is presented. Due to the properties of actual video coding standards, two strategies can be utilized for parallelization, data distribution and task distribution. To exploit the advantages of both approaches, a combination of the named strategies is used in the proposed hierarchical multiprocessor architecture. For optimization of the architecture, an efficiency measure is introduced which considers processing time, silicon area, and the yield of the semiconductor process. Results are given for an implementation example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fuzzy logic functions synthesis-A CMOS current mirror based solution
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The prototype framework is presented for automated synthesis/layout generation of current-mode fuzzy logic circuits using an intelligent module approach. The library of modules representing the standard fuzzy logic operators is built. These modules are used to synthesize sophisticated fuzzy logic units. Fuzzy unit designs are made on the results of current-mirror-based fuzzy logic function synthesis. This methodology is incorporated into the presented framework. As an example, the membership function unit is synthesized and the final layout is generated. A fuzzy logic based controller is described. The results show the advantages of the proposed system over the classical design methodology with respect to area, relative error and performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Continuous-time leapfrog filter with precise successive approximation tuning
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The design of a tunable continuous-time active-RC leapfrog filter whose precise response is controlled by means of a novel successive approximation tuning technique independent of tight circuit components matching. An RLC prototype ladder is described, together with the tunable active-RC leapfrog architecture. Experimental results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation of networks with inconsistent initial conditions
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method for the handling of numerically inconsistent initial conditions in networks with ideal switches is described. The use of the backward Euler formula is discussed, and emphasis is placed on easy understanding and easy programming applications. It is shown that in switched networks nonlinear storage elements must be defined by charges and fluxes; if not used, incorrect results are obtained for any step size. The methods have application in situations where initial conditions are consistent.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Chaos and bifurcations from a serial resonant circuit including a saturated inductor
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors analyze a periodically forced serial resonant circuit which includes a two-segment piecewise linear inductor. In some idealized case, the one-dimensional return map can be derived exactly. This mapping can give a theoretical explanation for an interesting route from a periodic response to chaos. In this route, the coexistence of attractors is confirmed. Also, this mapping can explain observable chaos generation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Gate array placement based on mincut partitioning with path delay constraints
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Two placement methods for VLSI gate array layout considering interconnection delay are proposed. One is a fast iterative improvement algorithm, and the other is a simulated-annealing-based algorithm. Both the proposed methods directly treat timing constraints, each of which is given to a pair of pins in the circuit. Experimental results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Initiability: A Measure Of Sequential Testability
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The testing of sequential circuit is difficult when problems occur concerning setting their initial state and checking their final state after test. The initiability measure is shown to be an efficient means for the quantification of the initialization problem of a sequential circuit. Test point insertion for sequential circuits based on the proposed modeling technique and the initiability concept is discussed. The technique for selecting the appropriate flip-flops for inclusion into partial scan is described. For all experiments, the initiability analysis is performed by the tool for sequential testability analysis (TOSTA).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Graph & network theory and cellular mobile communications
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors review the application of graph and network theory to mobile communication, especially, to channel assignment problems in cellular systems. Recently, two types of coloring problems on graphs or networks related to the channel assignment problem were proposed. These coloring problems are introduced. Some results on these problems are shown. The relation between cell structure and the Voronoi diagram is considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Efficient test vectors for ISCAS sequential benchmark circuits
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The sequential automatic test pattern generation system FASTEST is implemented with new heuristics to produce efficient test vectors for sequential circuits. The efficiency of FASTEST in terms of the quality of test vectors is demonstrated. The test vectors provide excellent fault coverage by fairly short test sequences. The profile of the ISCAS benchmark circuits is also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A sequential algorithm for robust parameter estimation and enhancement of noisy speech
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The sequential estimation of robust parameters and enhancement of noisy speech based on the expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm is considered when the excitation source is a mixture of two Gaussian distributions with different variances. Methods of stochastic approximation are used to convert a traditionally iterative algorithm into a sequential one. The proposed algorithm is robust against the observation noise and enhances noisy speech to produce results that are 3/spl sim/4-dB better than conventional methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Systolic array for 2D circular convolution using the Chinese remainder theorem
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new systolic array is proposed for efficient implementation of two dimensional (2-D) circular convolution (CC). It performs the Chinese remainder theorem in two index coordinates in order to avoid the need of broadcasting inputs to all cells and circular communication between the cells. The array is modular with nearest neighbor communication, and it is suitable for VLSI implementation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A neural network approach for robust dynamical control of robot manipulators
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new algorithm for adaptive dynamical control of robot manipulators is proposed. It utilizes a reduced order parameterization together with a computed torque control policy. The teaching signal correlates the total torque with the feedback error. The algorithm was simulated for a three revolute joint robot and various factors such as noisy joint velocity measurements, weaker control, persistency of excitation and choice of learning constants are examined. Implementation issues for parallel processing are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low-voltage low-power amplifiers
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Low-voltage and low-power amplifiers are strongly limited in dynamic range (DR) and bandwidth (B). The maximum dynamic-range/supply-power ratio is restricted to DR/sub max//P/sub sup/ = /spl pi//16 kTBe by thermal noise in resistors. To obtain this maximum value, several rail-to-rail (R-R) input stages and R-R output stages biased in class-AB are designed. The maximum bandwidth/supply-power ratio is restricted to B/sub 0max//P/sub sup/ = 3/C/sub L/V/sub sup/, and B/sub 0max//P/sub sup/ = 1/120I/sup 1/2//sub D/C/sub L/V/sub sup/, respectively, for bipolar and CMOS transistors. To obtain this maximum value at a sufficient amount of low-frequency gain, several compensation structures are designed, such as parallel, Miller, and multipath nested Miller compensation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reducing the complexity of FIR filters by using parallel structures
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A novel structure to implement narrow as well as moderately wide transition width computationally efficient finite impulse response (FIR) filters is presented. The structure yields 20%-40% savings in the number of multipliers for moderately wide transition-width filters. The saving for the narrow transition-width filters increases with decreasing transition-width.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic adaptive contrast enhancement for radiological imaging
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Enhancement of radiological images can improve their subsequent clinical interpretation or improve their automatic screening. Two new algorithms for automated adaptive contrast enhancement are presented. Compared to existing techniques, the proposed methods are completely automatic, in the sense that they do not require any interactive iterative adjustments by the reviewing physician. They exhibit better or equal performance with available methods. Both algorithms can be efficiently implemented using low-cost workstations or personal computers and can process even 2K /spl times/ 2K images in a few seconds.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Estimation of range-Doppler radar images
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: It is shown that most accurate reconstruction of a range-Doppler target density that can be computed from N waveforms and their echoes is obtained by transmitting the singular functions corresponding to the N largest singular values of two kernels derived from the target density. The singular functions are valid wavelets that obey an additional orthogonality constraint in the frequency domain. Using this result, a solution is discussed for the problem of choosing a set of N waveforms to reconstruct with high accuracy an arbitrary unknown target range-Doppler density function.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EOG segmentation using fast algorithms
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new method is presented for segmentation of rapidly time-varying signals based on fast least squares algorithms, due to their low complexity. The detection test used is based on the likelihood variable which appears explicitly in the fast algorithms. In order to show the performances of the method, it is applied to E.O.G. (electrooculograms) signals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A BiCMOS dynamic divider circuit using a nonrestoring iterative architecture with carry look ahead for CPU VLSI
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A race-free BiCMOS dynamic divider circuit using a non-restoring iterative architecture with carry look ahead is presented. Using the BiCMOS dynamic circuit, an 8-bit /spl divide/ 4-bit divider test circuit, based on 2-/spl mu/m BiCMOS technology, shows more than 4.5 times improvement in speed as compared to the CMOS divider circuit. The speed advantage of the BiCMOS dynamic divider circuit is even greater in a 64-bit divider, which is helpful for CPU VLSI.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The algebra of system design: A Petri net model of modular composition
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A mathematically-based CAD system is being designed. The system will have a predicate logic theorem prover at its core, and will mirror every surface-level design step with an internal proof-step. Verification proofs will be byproducts of the design process: that is, circuits designed in this system will already be proven to be correct implementations of their specifications. However, an insistence that everything be expressed in pure predicate logic is as frequently obfuscating as it is clarifying: some aspects of circuit requirements and design descriptions cannot easily be expressed in logic. Allowing different expressions to infiltrate the proof-based CAD environment could destroy the mathematical integrity of the system. To protect the system while allowing more flexible descriptions, different models were used for expressing and reasoning about different requirements. The framework for the safe integration of these various models is a general-purpose composition algebra. The authors impart some of the flavor of the algebra by describing the mathematics; presenting a simple gate-level example; and, principally, by working through a relatively substantial Petri Net example. The Petri net example demonstrates that some important aspects of hardware specification and design that can only be expressed with great difficulty in other formal models of concurrency can be expressed almost effortlessly in the algebra.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A quadratic-constrained least-squares approach to linear phase orthonormal filter bank design
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The design of M-channel paraunitary linear-phase filter banks is considered. It is shown that the symmetry polarities of linear-phase filters must be a particular pattern if the filters have narrow transition band and high stopband attenuation. The general design problem is formulated as a quadratic-constrained optimization problem which offers fast convergence. An example is given to demonstrate the theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Canonical PWL network and multilayer perceptron-like networks: A unified view
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors consider the behavior of the most popular type of mapping networks, the multilayer perceptron-like (MLPL) networks in implementing or approximating functions, in terms of the canonical piecewise-linear (PWL) functions. They show that a MLPL network may be understood as performing a canonical PWL function or a PWL function which is a composition of the canonical PWL functions. The discussion further suggests a generalized class of the canonical-PWL (CPWL) networks, i.e., networks which perform a canonical PWL function or a composition of the canonical PWL functions, which includes all layered feedforward networks where the nonlinearity of the units is represented or approximately represented by a PWL function.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive algorithm for discontinuity preserving image restoration
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Conventional adaptive algorithms for image restoration tend to blur the image by smoothing over discontinuities. To overcome this, a discontinuity preserving adaptive algorithm (DPAA) for image restoration is developed. The basic idea is to combine the continuous line field model with the usual linear finite impulse response (FIR) model used for image restoration. The constructed cost function is minimized using the gradient descent algorithm in adaptive setup. Computational cost and simulation results are given to aid comparison of DPAA and the conventional 2-D least mean square (LSD) algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A BiCMOS tunable shaper for detectors of elementary particles
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A BiCMOS biquadratic continuous-time filter is presented. The cell has been designed as 'noise shaper' for signal processing in the electronic read-out channel of elementary particles detectors. The network synthesizes a semi-Gaussian response where the shaping time (nominally 20 ns) and the quality factor (nominally 1/2) can be externally adjusted to realize the desired transient response. A linearity error lower than 1% is achieved for step input signal amplitudes up to 240 mV. The input referred noise is about 40 nV//spl radic/Hz, and the total current consumption is 200 /spl mu/A.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Models for nonlinear transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Transmission line models are discussed which arise by spatial discretization with different integration rules of the first order. Several circuit models for both linear and nonlinear lossless wave equations are presented. The quality in the linear case is evaluated by a comparison of network properties like reciprocity, symmetry, losslessness and non-minimum-phase property with the analytic solution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A model for VLSI implementation of CNN image processing chips using current-mode techniques
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A new cellular neural network model is proposed. It allows simpler and faster VLSI implementation than previous models. Current-mode building blocks are presented for the design of CMOS image preprocessing chips (feature extraction, noise filtering, compound component detection, etc.) using the cellular neural network paradigm. Area evaluation for the new model shows a reduction of about 50% as compared to the use of current-mode techniques with conventional models. Experimental measurements of CMOS prototypes designed in a 1.6-/spl mu/m n-well double-metal single-poly technology are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A neural network model for nonlinear predictive coding in Fock space
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A generic nonlinear autoregressive (AR) model for a random time series is presented. The model is obtained by a nonlinear predictive coding (NLPC) approach which expresses the minimum mean square error estimate of the current value of the series as a Volterra series in terms of its immediate N preceding values. This Volterra series is assumed to belong to a generalized Fock Hilbert space F. In the second stage, which is parametric, the model parameters, which are coefficients of a linear combination of known nonlinear random functions of the data, are obtained by linear mean square estimation. The implementations of the model and of the estimator appear respectively as two layer recurrent and feedforward neural networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of entropy-constrained RVQ to coding image subbands
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A recent study on the application of entropy constrained residual vector quantization (EC-RVQ) to subband image coding is discussed. The newly introduced EC-RVQ has produced excellent performance results when applied directly to coding images, and is also more cost efficient than competing vector quantization (VQ) methods which have so far been reported in the literature. Experimental results show that subband coding with EC-RVQ performs very well, and place it among the best techniques presently available in terms of performance. A discussion of the new system is given, and some performance comparisons are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new edge detection algorithm: Fast and localizing to a single pixel
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Commonly used methods of edge detection are unable to localize the edges to single pixel, and hence yield thick lines. Edge detection by Haar transform is investigated. The method can localize the edge to single pixels, and its computational complexity is lower than the Sobel operator method by a factor of more than two. The Haar transform method is as efficient as other methods for curved edges, and visibly better for straight edges.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Continuous-time common-mode feedback networks for fully-differential amplifiers: a comparative study
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Suitable figures of merit to compare different common-mode feedback (CMFB) networks are deduced. They allow evaluation of the conversion gain or linear interaction, relative performance, and nonlinear interaction between common-mode and differential-mode loops in any fully differential one-stage output compensated amplifier. Three often used CMFB loops, based on different operation principles, are classified according to these figures of merit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Character recognition using neural based feature extractor and classifier
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present a neural network architecture for the recognition of handwritten digits and machine printed multi-font characters. To reduce the dimension of the input data vector as well as robustness of the system, an appropriate neural net is utilized for the feature extraction part which is cascaded with another neural net for the classification purpose. The proposed architecture has been tested on a large sample of real field data and the results indicate the effectiveness of the proposed technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A near optimal algorithm for image compression using Gabor expansion
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The Gabor expansion is studied for the purpose of image compression. The mathematical conditions required to obtain complete sets of Gabor functions in L/sub 2/(R) are presented. The concept of Gabor expansion is further interpreted in terms of the compression of real digital images. The problems of both complete and partial Gabor expansions of images are stated, and an optimization algorithm which provides the iterative algorithm, based on the conjugate gradient algorithm, converges in a finite number of iterations and it is not computationally too costly (O(n/sup 2/) calculations per iteration). For complete expansions, a new and tight bound on the number of iterations required to achieve exact reconstructions is given. For partial expansions, it is shown that very good reconstructed images can be obtained with bit rates as low as 0.6 bit per pixel.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design techniques aimed at 3 volt CMOS delta sigma converters
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The growing importance of 3-volt digital CMOS applications is creating a real need for 3-volt mixed signal devices. The importance of oversampled analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog converters in these mixed signal devices necessitates their integration into 3-volt systems. Some of the issues are outlined, and several approaches are presented that may yield solutions for various applications in a 1.0-/spl mu/ CMOS technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Suppression of acoustic oscillations in hearing aids using minimum phase techniques
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Minimum phase equalization techniques used to suppress acoustic oscillations in hearing aid systems are described. Minimum phase equalization techniques cancel a substantial fraction of the open loop phase delay and make it easy to use other techniques to suppress acoustic oscillations. Some design examples, together with computer simulation results, are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ELT-based wavelet coding of high-fidelity audio signals
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An audio coder capable of high-fidelity representation of audio signals (sampled at 44.1 kHz) at a rate of 2.5 bits/sample is presented. The coder is based on a wavelet transform with frequency resolutions varying from 21.5 Hz to 344 Hz, and time resolutions varying from 23.2 ms to 1.45 ms. With this multiresolution approach, two benefits result. The preecho effect for high-frequency transients is virtually eliminated, and the wavelet transform has a computational complexity that is 15% lower than that of the commonly used block transform.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Throughput analysis in timed colored Petri nets
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: It is shown that the steady-state behavior of a class of timed colored Petri nets can be analyzed by using the concept of throughput and simple rules of operational analysis. Since such analysis is based on the average value of firing times rather than firing time distribution functions, the same approach can be applied to a variety of net models. Throughput analysis is based on structural properties of nets only, so it avoids the potential complexity of reachability analysis, and can be used for analysis of unbounded nets.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Object-oriented representation, analysis, and scheduling of signal transition graphs
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present components of a design environment for specification and validation of asynchronous communication protocols. As novel contributions they propose an object-oriented foundation of the design environment and efficient algorithms for the signal transition graphs used as high-level specifications of communication protocols. These algorithms validate important properties of cyclic graphs as required to synthesize correctly logic circuits from protocol specifications. Results are presented for initial marking and scheduling validation of protocol specifications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Efficient sensitivity analysis for large nonideal switched capacitor networks
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new sensitivity analysis method in the frequency domain is presented for nonideal switched capacitor networks. The method is more general and efficient than previously published works. There are no restrictions on the number of clock phases, circuit configuration and input signal type (which can be either continuous or sample-and-hold). By performing a substantial amount of frequency-independent preprocessing, and by using adjoint network techniques, the computational costs are reduced, and a highly efficient method results. The method is implemented in a switched capacitor (SC) network analysis program called SCNAP4. Numerical results of the sensitivity analysis of a fifth-order elliptic low pass filter are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Broadband lossless monolithic microwave floating active inductor
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A broadband, lossless microwave active floating inductor is proposed for general use in a monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC). The features of this active floating inductor are that: (i) it is lossless; (ii) it can operate over a wide microwave frequency range; (iii) its size is independent of the inductance value; and (iv) it can be easily realized in MMIC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Histogram-shape preserving algorithm for image enhancement
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new direct contrast enhancement algorithm is proposed. It can be used to enhance the contrast of an image without increasing the dynamic range of the pixel values. A distinctive property of the proposed method is that it yields results matching the characteristic of the human visual system. The histogram of the enhanced image has almost the same shape as that of the original image.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the performance of augmented signature testing
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Signature registers are widely used to compact test Data In Built-in Self-test (BIST) environments. Closed form expressions are obtained for aliasing probability in augmented signature testing which uniquely identifies the quotient, under both generalized independent and q-ary symmetric error models for arbitrary test lengths.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High speed buffers for op-amp characterization
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Techniques for testing the frequency response of an operational amplifier (op-amp) sometimes require a buffer in the feedback path. This buffer is needed to prevent an inadvertent forward signal path from the input of the op-amp to the output of the op-amp through the feedback circuitry. The buffer must have very good linearity and a higher bandwidth than the op-amp under test. Three CMOS buffer designs are presented. Simulation results show total harmonic distortion of about 1% at frequencies as high as 10 MHz into a load capacitance at 5 pF. The buffers settle to within 1% of the final voltage in fewer than 20 ns.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Feature based compression of vector quantized codebooks and data for optimal image compression
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The Linde-Buzo-Gray (LBG) algorithm is a procedure in vector quantization. An attempt is made to compress the LBG codebook by simple feature-based clustering. The centroids of the resulting clusters form a reduced LBG codebook. The resulting reduced LBG codebook has almost identical SNR as the equivalent size original LBG codebook. Several other experimental results are presented which show that the above clustering technique may be applied directly to the original images in order to find an initial codebook for LBG codebook training, or to quickly generate an alternative codebook with comparable quality.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimal reactive power dispatch with fuzzy variables
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors present a consistent treatment of the optimal reactive power dispatch problem taking into account the uncertainty associated with load values. Linguistic declarations of loads are translated into possibility distribution functions via fuzzy sets. The problem is decomposed into four subproblems via Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition for reducing the problem dimensions. Voltage constraints within each subproblem are modeled via fuzzy sets to bias the final solution toward the static security region. A numerical example is presented to demonstrate the applicability of the method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of a multiresolution optical-flow-based method for motion estimation to video coding
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An iterative multiresolution method based on finite elements for estimating the optical flow is presented and applied to video coding. The computed motion field is smooth and can be represented by a small number of finite-element coefficients. Preliminary simulation results are encouraging, as good quality estimates are obtained for the Salesman sequence.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Redundant algebra and integrated circuit implementation of ternary logic and their applications
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A new algebra called redundant algebra is proposed and analyzed for the design of the ternary logic systems. The ternary systems can be realized by dynamic CMOS logic circuits. A new dynamic differential logic called CMOS redundant differential logic (CRDL) is developed to increase the logic flexibility and the circuit performance. The multiplier with redundant binary addition (RBA) tree is designed in both synchronous and pipelined systems. The synchronous RBAs designed by using CRDL circuits show better speed performance than other proposed static RBAs. The pipelined multiplier designed by using the true-single-phase-clock (TSPC) scheme has higher operating frequency and less pipelined stages as compared to the conventional binary parallel pipelined multiplier. The experimental chip is fabricated and measured. This successfully verifies the correctness of the logic functions and the advantage in speed performance of the designed circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Generic face recognition, feature extraction and edge detection using optimal DSNR expansion matching
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Expansion matching optimizes a matching criterion called discriminative signal to noise ratio (DSNR) and has been shown to robustly recognize templates under conditions of noise, severe occlusion and superposition. The optimal DSNR matching filter for multiple templates is used to create a generic face filter, by requiring the designed filter to elicit equal responses to all the training faces. A new family of optimal DSNR edge detectors is introduced, based on the expansion filter of several edge models. The step edge detector is compared with the Canny edge detector (CED). Experimental comparisons show that the authors' edge detector is superior to the CED in terms of DSNR, even under very noisy signal conditions. Expansion matching is also successful in extracting features such as corners from images. Experimental results of corner extraction are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the use of orientation information for improved contour difference coding
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Contour difference coding represents Freeman chain codes using only the differences between consecutive links. Improved contour difference coding is possible through the use of information about the orientation of the links forming the differences. It is shown analytically that grid-intersect quantization of curves inherently results in different underlying probability distributions for diagonally and vertical-horizontally oriented chain differences. This difference can be exploited to produce models with reduced source entropy. Results are presented demonstrating the effectiveness of this method on real contour data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fully tunable GaAs MESFET OTA-C integrator suitable for high-precision continuous-time filtering
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Measured results for a novel operational transconductance amplifier (OTA)-C integrator realized in 0.5-/spl mu/m, -1-V threshold GaAs MESFET technology are presented. A wide tuning range and high levels of DC gain are achieved using a single geometry device (20 /spl mu/m), and without reliance on early saturation. Total harmonic distortion (THD) level are quite modest and show good agreement with SPICE simulations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A class of zero wasted area floorplan for VLSI design
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A new approach to solve the floorplan area optimization problem is proposed. Using the analogy between a floorplan and a resistive network, the length and width of an individual block of a floorplan are represented by the voltage and current of a branch in a resistive network of a certain topology. The floorplan area minimization problem becomes a resistive network synthesis problem with a given power dissipation. By applying network and graph theories, a systematic network analogy procedure is developed. Necessary and sufficient conditions for zero wasted area floorplan are also given. An optimal algorithm for solving the optimization problem is proposed by replacing the nonlinear equations with the linear ones. Experimental results show that the authors' algorithm is efficient and can handle a large floorplan successfully.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel current mode winner-take-all circuit for artificial neural networks
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors describe the use of a switched-current concept in realizing a winner-take-all circuit for artificial neural networks. Unlike other conventional winner-take-all networks the new approach displays no inhibition between neurons but rather allows the neurons to compete among themselves. Equations governing the operation as well as its limitations are presented and verified through simulations. Control logic is required making this circuit fully compatible with the mixed analog/digital integrated technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High compression ratio image compression
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An image compression method is proposed. It makes use of the wavelet transform (WT) with better frequency localization and the adaptive hierarchical vector quantization (AHVQ) technique. The WT provides a multifrequency channel representation for the image from which proper coding methods can be drawn. The AHVQ technique lowers the bit rate significantly while causing no extra distortion and little extra computation. Experimental results with compression ratios of up to 100: 1 are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 3V high-frequency current-mode filters
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A fully differential current mode integrator circuit and its cascode variants are presented for use in low voltage, high frequency signal processing applications. It is shown that good linearity is achieved with signal levels up to the current bias, the equivalent of voltage mode rail-to-rail operation. It is also shown that low (voltage) bias levels actually improve linearity (within the strong inversion region of operation), enabling bias levels to be designed low enough for the integrators to work at 3V supply voltages. Major frequency response barriers are eliminated because the basic integrator has by design no parasitic poles, which enables the frequency of operation to scale much higher than previously practical. The design, fabrication, and characterization of a test filter demonstrated the feasibility of the approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital correction for improved spectral response in signal generation systems
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Signal generation systems using direct digital synthesis (DDS) techniques are marked by flexibility, repeatability, and wide range of stable operating frequencies. The spectral accuracy of these systems is limited by the analog components used to convert the signal into continuous-time. It is demonstrated how the addition of digital signal processing and a feedback loop around the analog signal path can increase the spectral quality.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Noncausal image modeling with applications to image restoration
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The problem of noncausal image modeling and estimation with applications to image restoration is considered. The noncausal vector autoregressive model for the image process is arranged into a descriptor system. This system is then decomposed into forward and backward stable subsystems which capture the dynamic behavior of the original descriptor system. The design of a time-varying filter is considered. The forward state is estimated, with the backward state considered as a colored output noise. The backward state is estimated, with the forward state regarded as colored output noise. Simulation results for noncausal image modeling are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A parallel force direct based VLSI standard cell placement algorithm
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new heuristic algorithm is described. It can be used to minimize the weighted wire length in the placement of modules in VLSI chips. A salient feature of PIREN2.0 is that multiple permutations based upon the connectivity between the modules are made simultaneously on all modules in order to minimize the objective function. This allows the algorithm, without major modifications, to be mapped to a processor array structure, the MasPar MP-2.2. Each processor in this massively parallel single instruction, multiple data (SIMD) machine can perform in parallel the computation necessary to place cells in an optimum relative location to one another based upon the connectivity (the number of wires) between cells. A speedup for the benchmark circuits of at least 7.5 is obtained from the parallel version without degrading the quality of the layout solution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new strategy for library-independent layout design
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new strategy for layout synthesis is presented. The general gate array design system (GGADS) system which uses the strategy has been implemented and is capable of designing layouts for configurable gate array master structures. GGADS evaluates the effectiveness of layouts on gate array master. It supports the development of special purpose gate array master structures. GGADS is suitable for the layout of circuits which are not tractable by library-based approaches, e.g., ECL logic.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An adaptive network for blind separation of independent signals
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The problem of separating two or several independent signals (or independent speakers) from an array of sensors within the framework of adaptive systems is formulated. The delayed signals are modeled as a dynamic state model. The crucial aspect of this formulation is to quantify the property of independence of signals in terms of an explicit function to be optimized. Then, the derived adaptive dynamics will work to minimize (or maximize) the explicit function. The convergence of this newly derived adaptive scheme is shown. As the dynamics converge, the network will succeed in identifying the mixing and the delays in the original signals, and will reproduce the original independent signals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A method for improving the efficiency of simulating large electronic circuits
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The efficiency of a circuit simulator can be measured in terms of its simulation speed and memory usage requirements. Rather than working with numerical integration, sparse matrix, and network equation formulation techniques to improve simulation efficiency, the effects of circuit topology of the built-in models on the simulation efficiency are investigated. A new model transformation technique is developed and implemented in a simulation program with IC emphasis (SPICE)-like program. Experimental results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new zero-current-switching constant switching frequency boost converter
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors present a new boost topology which can be operated in constant switching frequency and zero-current-switching. In addition, the voltage stresses on the active switches are as low as the traditional boost pulse width modulated (PWM) converter. The control curves are derived through the normalized state-plane trajectory. The design procedure is given through a specific example. Simulation waveforms are provided to verify the analytical results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A transconductor-capacitor video filter and equaliser design
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A design technique for a ladder-based transconductor-capacitor (transconductor-C) lowpass video filter and equalizer is presented. The software package for a general transconductor-C filter and equalizer design is described. A fifth-order elliptic lowpass filter and a sixth-order group delay equalizer are designed. It is shown that the order of the equalizer can be reduced by the application of special techniques for the approximation of the filter transfer function. The comparison of sensitivity between a cascade of biquadratic stages and the ladder-based realization is given. Lower sensitivities to component tolerance for both filter and equalizer are displayed by the ladder-based design. The fifth-order amplitude and sixth-order group delay equalizer are incorporated in a layout for fabrication.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the design of a doubly-matched (D-M) diplexer with a common junction
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Two sets of formulas and a three-stage computer aided approach are presented for the design of a doubly-matched (D-M) diplexer composed of two channel equalizers connected either in parallel or in series at a common junction. The diplexer provides a good match between a complex generator impedance and two complex channel loads. It is known as the doubly-matched (D-M) diplexer. A design example of a D-M diplexer is given to demonstrate the approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computation of static stability margins in power systems using monotonicity
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The load-generation margins are calculated for given phase angle safety limits based on the decoupled real power-phase angle (P-/spl theta/) load-flow equations. If a load or generator remains within the computed margins, the phase angles are guaranteed to stay within the safety limits, since the method is based on equivalent circuits and monotonicity relations and does not involve any linear approximation. Furthermore, the method allows direct identification of the critical transmission line for the power variation at a given load or generator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Blind deconvolution of linear systems driven by non-stationary source based on almost-symmetrical time-varying ARMA model
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Two blind convolution schemes based on an almost-symmetrical time-varying autoregressive moving average (ARMA) model are proposed. Such a model is constructed for analytical source signals. Blind deconvolution of two categories of sources (constant-envelope and time-varying envelope) are discussed. The uniqueness of the blind deconvolution is shown to be guaranteed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modified probabilistic RAM architecture for VLSI implementation of a backpropagation learning algorithm
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A network based on the modified probabilistic RAM architecture is proposed for VLSI implementation with on-chip learning capability. The pRAM structure is modified for the computation of error backpropagation and weight updates, where the multiplication and summations are performed with simple AND gates and OR gates, respectively. The simulation results for the derived algorithm are discussed, and a VLSI implementation of the pRAM for backpropagation is also explained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital circuit implementation of a continuous-time inference network for the transitive closure problem
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A class of binary relation inference networks has been proposed for solving constraint satisfaction and optimization problems, especially those related with time/location-referencing and shortest path applications. An important extension of this type of network is described. It provides an efficient solution to the transitive closure problem. For a given N-node directed graph problem, the inference network consists of N(N-1) interconnected units, where (N-2) sites are attached to each of these units. Simple binary AND operation is required at each site. Each unit performs an (N-1)-input OR operation. The computation has a time complexity bounded by a scalar multiple of log/sub 2/(N-1), and can be executed in the continuous-time domain. Theoretical analysis on network convergence is discussed. Numerical simulation of a digital circuit implementation indicates a solution time in the time range of nanoseconds.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the practical BIBO stability of multidimensional filters
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The conventional definition of multidimensional (m-D) bounded-input bounded-output (BIBO) stability permits the m-D domain of the input signal, and of the m-D computations, to be of infinite extent in all m-dimensions. The definition of m-D practical-BIBO (P-BIBO) stability restricts the m-D domain of the input signal, and of the computations, to be of finite extent in all but one of the m dimensions. It is shown that the P-BIBO stability criterion corresponds to those computations that can be made with a machine having a finite number of (infinite-precision) memory storage elements, whereas the BIBO stability criterion, which is more restrictive, also includes machines having an infinite number of (infinite-precision) memory storage elements. It is argued that the extension of the BIBO stability criterion to include such infinitely large machines is of limited practical value, and that P-BIBO stability is the more useful criterion, and is easier to test.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved Chen-Smith image coder
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An image compression system based on transform coding and zonal sampling is presented. It is based on the Chen-Smith coder, but with an improved technique for transform coefficient quantization and the replacement of the discrete cosine transform (DCT) by the lapped orthogonal transform (LOT). The system leads to signal-to-noise ratios that are from 1.5 to 2.0 dB above those obtained with the standard JPEG algorithm, for a wide variety of test images and compression rates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new schematic-driven floorplanning algorithm for analog cell layout
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A new schematic-driven floorplanning algorithm is described. This algorithm improves on initial constructive placement iteratively not only by selecting the best orientation for the module cells, but also by optimizing the floorplan topology through local transformations applied to the polar graph representation of the floorplan. The transformations are easy to implement, efficient to perform and produce compact layout.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the relationship between negative differential resistance and stability for nonlinear one-ports
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors derive a fundamental relationship, for a nonlinear one-port, between the presence of negative differential resistance across the port at a particular DC operating point and the stability of that operating point. In particular, they illustrate that the presence of negative differential resistance does not necessarily imply instability for all possible resistive port terminations but that it does imply instability for either an open-circuit or a short-circuit termination.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Lossless compression for medical imaging systems using linear/nonlinear prediction and arithmetic coding
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A differential pulse code modulation (DPCM)-based system is proposed for lossless compression of medical images. Three techniques are used in the system. The intensity of the current pixel is predicted optimally by linear combination of the intensities of N pixels in a neighborhood of the causal region. The multilayer perceptron, a feedforward neural network, is used to model the nonlinearity in images. A hierarchical prediction scheme is adapted for progressive transmission. Coefficients for each hierarchical layer are chosen optimally to achieve minimum entropy. Prediction errors, assumed to be Laplacian distributed, are encoded by the Q-coder, an adaptive arithmetic coder.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A computationally efficient second order adaptive lattice filter
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A nonlinear second order Volterra filter can be reformulated as a linear multichannel lattice structure. Such a formulation reduces eigenvalue disparity for gradient descent adaptive implementations. For a filter of memory span L, this approach requires O(L/sup 3/) coefficients, with corresponding computational burden and memory requirements. A more efficient two-stage lattice structure is described, where a similar result is achieved with computational complexity proportional to O(L/sup 2/).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Signal detection by using higher order statistics
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The performance of a traditional energy-based detector relies finally on signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). To improve the detection performance of the weak non-Gaussian signal embedded in Gaussian noise, both the third order and the second order statistics of the observed data are used to construct a two-channel detector. The performance of the two-channel detector is significantly improved as long as the bispectrum of the observed data are sufficiently large.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Applications of 3D LCR networks in the design of 3D recursive filters
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Applications of three-dimensional (3-D) LCR prototype filters in the design of 3-D recursive filters are proposed, including 3-D planar-rejection (PR) filters and 3-D planar-pass/planar-rejection (PP-PR) filters. A typical application of the 3-D PR filters is to reject spatial-dynamic or spatial-static background linear-trajectory component signals. A technique for implementing the 3-D filters is proposed that employs 3-D operators. A simple design procedure is described, having efficient modular 3-D filter structures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CMOS digital retina chip with multi-bit neurons for image coding
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors describe a CMOS digital retina chip with neurons having multi-bit output for image coding from analog to digital formats. The neuron having a 1-bit output model can easily be implemented by the use of CMOS inverters. It has individual digital inputs, a common quantized output and a comparator. The weight vector is given as a fixed numerical value by a channel conductance for pull-up PMOS and pull-down NMOS transistors, respectively. The delayed binary outputs of neurons in the neighborhood are directly connected to the digital inputs. The next state of the network is computed from the current state at some neurons in any time interval. To reduce the error between the input analog gray image and the output digital image, a two-bit image coding method is proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reducing the physical design cycle by means of topological placement with hard timing restraints
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new concept for topological module placement satisfying hard timing restraints based on segmenting the layout surface into topological rings is introduced. By using this method it is possible to shorten the layout-extraction-relayout cycle significantly, because the resulting placement satisfies user defined signal run-times. The new method can be applied to hierarchical layout systems, and is flexible in terms of design styles and module specifications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pipelined analog multi-layer feedforward neural networks
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Two methods for pipelining analog or hybrid neural networks with analog outputs are presented. These methods provide concurrent operation of various stages on different sets of the network input stream. A new analog neuron with an embedded latch for implementation of one of the architectures is also presented. These methods are particularly attractive for time-multiplexed implementation of multi-layer neural networks. It is shown that significant speed improvement can be achieved by these methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Image restoration by inhomogeneous G-M field modeling and adaptive Kalman filtering
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An inhomogeneous Gauss-Markov (G-M) model of the image field is used to enhance the visual quality of the restored image by Kalman filtering in the spatial domain. In the corresponding Kalman filter, the transition matrix in the predicting part is no longer a constant matrix as it was in previous homogeneous G-M modeling. Instead, it becomes a function of the spatial coordinates as well as the edge running parameter /spl theta/. The optimal estimate is a weighted sum of several Kalman filter estimates with each Kalman filter operating in parallel with a separate known value of /spl theta/. The experimental results are compared with those obtained in the homogeneous G-M modeling.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An analog smart sensor for active obstacle detection
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An analog smart sensor for active obstacle detection in the future intelligent automobile is presented. It integrates the entire optoelectronic portion of the active obstacle detection system, from image acquisition to laser spot position coding, on a single silicon die. A 64-pixel prototype circuit has been designed and fabricated in a 3 /spl mu/m CMOS process. Some test results are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Frequency estimation of sinusoids in colored noise
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A maximum a posteriori estimator of complex sinusoids in colored Gaussian noise is proposed. The unknown noise covariance matrix and the complex amplitudes of the sinusoids are of no interest, and therefore are not estimated. The observed data vectors are decomposed into signal and noise components. From the probability density functions of these components, using Bayes' rule, the marginal a posteriori density of the frequencies, and the proposed estimator are found. Computer simulations show excellent results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On coupled oscillators networks-For the cellular neural network
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors propose two types of coupled oscillator networks and investigate their steady states. One network has a two-dimensional honeycomb structure. The other network has a two-dimensional lattice structure. In the honeycomb circuit, three adjacent oscillators are coupled by one coupling resistor and it is considered that the voltages of three oscillators around a coupling resistor result in three-phase synchronization. In the lattice circuit, four-oscillators are coupled by one coupling resistor and it is considered that the voltages of four oscillators around a coupling resistor result in four-phase synchronization. As a result, the networks are expected to generate various synchronization patterns. In the networks each oscillator is connected to only its adjacent oscillators and various patterns are generated according to the initial condition. Therefore, the network is expected to be utilized as a cellular neural network in the future.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parallel converter systems with maximum current limit control scheme for reliability improvement
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A control strategy for improving parallel converter system reliability is proposed. This control combines the central-limit control with a maximum current limit and a fault-tolerance control feature to increase the degree of converter redundancy. This schedule assumes that the system consists of converter modules (CMs) operated in a continuous conduction mode, a current reference generator, and a system controller. There is no interconnection between CMs. Also, because each individual CM is directly controlled by the system controller, its failure can be detected and approximate correction actions can be given subsequently. Moreover, the proposed scheme is capable of determining a required number of CMs in the active state for any load condition. Thus, the degree of redundancy in the system is increased significantly. Only a few converters are activated at light loads. Therefore, the number of spare CMs increases virtually and the overall system reliability and performance is increased. The comparison between the proposed and conventional approaches on the aspects of system reliability is presented. In this comparison, the merit of the proposed control strategy in improving system reliability is highlighted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A decision feedback equalizer utilizing higher-order correlation
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A decision feedback equalizer (DFE), which utilizes higher-order correlation (HOC) information available in the input vector of the DFE is proposed. Due to its better utilization of the available information, better performance is expected and then demonstrated from several respects. The capability of the proposed structure in forming nonlinear decision boundary is shown. Better mean-square error (MSE) performance is presented. Better bit-error rate (BER) performance is demonstrated. Less performance loss due to error propagation and less effect caused by improper parameter setting are observed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Genlocked digital overlay on a video signal
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The synchronization problems involved in mixing computer graphics with a video signal are outlined, and it is shown how two components solve them. The components, a video encoder and a genlocking digitizer facilitate overlays of digital computer graphics and/or text data onto a standard analog NTSC (National Television System Committee) or PAL baseband television signal. The mapping of the clock and subcarrier recovery algorithm and the video encoding procedure into the architectures of the two chips is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An adaptive method for consistent parameter estimation of a non-Gaussian MA process
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A new adaptive method of estimating the parameters of non-Gaussian, nonminimum phase moving average processes is proposed. The adaptive method is developed using a consistency-guaranteed equation system of higher order cumulants. These can provide consistent estimates of the parameters. Simulation results are provided to show the performance of the new adaptive method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Subharmonic entrainment of frequency in nonlinear three-phase circuits with symmetry
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors present several features of subharmonic oscillations in a symmetrical three-phase circuit, which consists of a wye-delta connected three-phase transformer, voltage sources, linear resistors and capacitors. The exciting characteristics of the transformer are nonlinear. To analyze subharmonic oscillations, the asymptotic method developed by M. N. Krylov, N. N. Bogoliubov and I. A. Mitropolsky is extended. Particular attention is paid to the zero-phase fluxinterlinkages. The results demonstrate that three modes of 1/3-subharmonic oscillation exist. One of them is generated symmetrically in three phases and two of them unsymmetrically in two phases. For 1/2-subharmonic oscillation, there are two modes which occur symmetrically in three phases.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fast stability test for multidimensional systems
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An efficient (polynomial time) algorithm which computes the determinant of a polynomial matrix is presented. The proposed algorithm uses a fast Fourier transform (FFT) from the viewpoint of polynomial interpolation. A polynomial time stability test algorithm for two-dimensional digital systems is obtained by combining the proposed method with the method of B. D. O. Anderson and E. I. July (1973) that of D. O. Siljak (1975) (IEEE Trans., Vol. AU-21, pp. 366-372, 1973; IEEE Trans., Vol. CAS-22, pp. 183-189, 1975).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Conditions for the existence and uniqueness of DC solutions of networks containing nonlinear OpAmps with ideal model
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The authors give necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of DC solutions of resistive networks containing nonlinear operational amplifiers with an ideal model. Sandberg, Willson and other authors, studying similar problems for devices with a non-ideal model, have proved the importance of two classes of matrices called class P/sub o/ and class P. Conditions are given in terms of these classes of matrices.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Double edge triggered devices: Speed and power constraints
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new set of double edge triggered flip-flops has been developed. It requires fewer transistors to implement than earlier designs. The energy consumption in the authors' double edge triggered flip-flops is shown to be lower than in single edge triggered (SET) flip-flops. This is demonstrated by architecture level analysis, circuit analysis and simulation techniques. The maximum data rate in double and single edge triggered flip-flops is also compared via simulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MSE filter design and spectrum parameterization by orthogonal FAM transform
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An orthonormal set of the frequency amplitude modulated (FAM) class of functions is used to produce a frequency domain FAM transform suitable for infinite impulse response (IIR) filter design with least squared error criterion. The orthonormal basis used is chosen to be effectively implemented by a set of identical second order allpass filters equipped with a common magnitude weighting. The allpass parameters (/spl theta/, r) are first adapted to the problem in order to get rapid convergence in the mean squared error (MSE). The results show that the new method produces IIR filters with the same or better (in MSE sense) frequency domain response than finite impulse response (FIR) filters with 5 to 7 times higher order. The method allows optimization of the group delay properties. There are three different ways to approximate linear phase characteristics in the IIR filters produced.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An improved quantization model for the finite precision LMS adaptive algorithm
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An improved model is presented for the analysis of the errors due to the finite word length digital implementation of the least-mean-square (LMS) algorithm. The new formulation takes into consideration the correlation between the correction term and the corresponding quantization error in the updating equation. Analytical expressions are derived for the MSE (mean-square error). This facilitates the determination of the gain constant required to obtain a desired level of residual MSE. The results are suitable for design purposes. Simulation results are presented which validate the theoretical model proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A sensor array for phase and amplitude detection of synchronous modulated light sources
publicationTitle: 1993 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A chip implementation is presented of a sensor array capable of measuring modulation phase and amplitude of a light source, without being disturbed by stronger surrounding static or out-of-band modulated light.
